lessons.title: Non-Fiction: The History of Money
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about money from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about money.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about money.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about the history/purpose of money.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about money at home.

lessons.title: Recognising Coins
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise all UK coins.
success_criteria: I can name each UK coin.
I can sort coins by value.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recognising all UK coins (1p to £2), discussing their features.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort and order coins by value, recording their names.
key_questions: Can you order coins from smallest to largest value?

differentiation.greater_depth: Recognise and order all coins including £1 and £2

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check on coin recognition before the money unit deepens — evidence for MATHS.MEA.

lessons.title: Writing a Shopping List
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple shopping list with prices.
success_criteria: I can write items on a list.
I can add a price to each item.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss items on a typical shopping list.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a shopping list with items and prices.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own shopping list with 3-4 items and prices.
key_questions: What price will you give each?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write a detailed list with 6+ items

lessons.assessment_notes: Note list-writing skill applied to a money context — evidence for ENG.W2.
lessons.plenary: Share shopping lists with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Help write a real shopping list at home.

lessons.title: Recognising Notes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise UK notes.
success_criteria: I can name each UK note.
I can say its value.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recognising UK notes (£5, £10, £20, £50), discussing their features and values.
lessons.independent_task: Children match notes to their values, recording their names.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recognition skill for notes, a Year 2 objective — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise recognising notes together if available, or look at pictures.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Money Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read money-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read money words.
I can read a sentence about money.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to money-themed words (e.g. 'coin', 'spend', 'save').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading money words over the week.

lessons.title: Totalling Coins and Notes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find the total value of a mixed set of coins and notes.
success_criteria: I can add coin values together.
I can find a total including notes.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding the total value of mixed coins and notes.
lessons.independent_task: Children find totals of given collections of coins/notes.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Total collections using coins only, up to £1
differentiation.greater_depth: Total collections including notes, up to £50

lessons.assessment_notes: Record totalling skill extended to include notes — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise totalling coins and notes together.

lessons.title: Role-Play Shop
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use money vocabulary in a role-play shopping scenario.
success_criteria: I can ask for the price of an item.
I can say how much money I have.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap money vocabulary learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a role-play shop scenario using money vocabulary.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns as shopkeeper and customer in a role-play shop, using money vocabulary.
key_questions: How much money do you have?

differentiation.greater_depth: Extend role-play with more complex transactions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and money vocabulary application — evidence for ENG.SL1/MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Play shop with your family using real or play coins.

lessons.title: Money Word Problems: Totals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve word problems finding the total cost of items.
success_criteria: I can solve a money word problem.
I can find the total cost.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap totalling coins and notes from Wednesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems finding the total cost of two or more items.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve money word problems, showing working.
key_questions: What is the total cost of these items?
How did you work it out?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record money problem-solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2/MEA.
lessons.home_link: Make up a money word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Money: Coins and Notes Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about money.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about money, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might we use notes instead of lots of coins?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on money facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Coins, Notes, Totals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply coin/note recognition and totalling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can recognise coins and notes.
I can find a total value.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of coin/note recognition and totalling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: recognition, totalling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 33 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising coin/note recognition over the weekend.
